paper.title: A Multi-Armed Bandit Approach for Online Expert Selection in Markov Decision Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed bandit approach to choosing experts in MDPs
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Arms are expert policies acting on a shared (partially observed) finite MDP whose state couples successive pulls; Markovian environment, out of scope under v0.5.
unmapped: Each arm (expert) is a stationary policy inducing an irreducible aperiodic Markov chain on a shared finite MDP; state carries over between pulls
Each pull runs the chosen expert for T_n MDP steps and observes the average reward
Regret compares to the steady-state average reward of the best expert
Learner (UCB) uses the mixing constants K_e = C_e/(1-alpha_e) of each expert's Markov chain
settings.definition_quote: The cumulative regret, $r(n)$ after $n$ iterations of a multi-armed bandit algorithm is defined as: \[r(n)=n\bar R^* -  \sum_{k = 0}^{n}\frac{1}{T_k}\sum_{t=t_k}^{t_{k+1}-1} r_t\]

algorithms.name: Any multi-armed bandit algorithm in the MAB approach to MDPs (Algorithm 1)
Upper Confidence Bounds for MDPs
requires_knowledge_of: K_e (mixing constants of each expert's induced Markov chain)

symbols.E_T_i: expected number of times suboptimal expert i is chosen in n iterations
symbols.C_i: mixing constant C_e of expert i's induced Markov chain
symbols.alpha_mix_i: geometric mixing rate alpha_e of expert i's chain

conditions: induced Markov chains of all experts irreducible and aperiodic

source.label: prop:rdi
source.quote: If the induced Markov chains for each expert $e \in \Ec$ are irreducible and aperiodic, then the expected cumulative regret at time $n$ can be bounded with: \E[r(n)]\le \sum_{e\ne e^*} \E[ T_e(n) ] \left[ \Delta_e + \frac{C_e}{T_0(1 -\alpha_e)} \right] + \frac{C_{*}}{1-\alpha_{*}}\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{T_k}

results.notes: Regret decomposition for any bandit algorithm; Delta_i is the steady-state reward gap. Regret defined vs. steady-state mean of best expert; in expectation it is pseudo-regret-like.

symbols.K_i: K_e = C_e/(1-alpha_e), mixing constant of expert i

conditions: induced Markov chains irreducible and aperiodic

source.label: prop:ucbregret
source.quote: For a set of experts $\Ec$ and initial time horizon $T_0$ such that $\bar{R^*}-\bar{R}^e > \frac{2K_e}{T_0}$ for all $e \in \Ec$, and for a choice of $\delta(n)=n^{-4}$, the expected regret of the UCB algorithm after $n$ time steps of the algorithm, $\E[r(n)]$, satisfies: ...

results.notes: Paper then notes with T_n = T_0 + c n the last term is at most (K_*/c) log((T_0+cn-c)/T_0), giving O(log n) regret (not a separate formal statement). Proof's correctness questionable (uses T_n in denominator), recorded as stated.
